text: For a square matrix A, a scalar λ is an eigenvalue precisely when:
choices: det(A − λI) = 0, i.e. λ is a root of the characteristic polynomial
Av = λv holds for every vector v
λ is a nonzero vector satisfying Av = λv
explanation: The book defines eigenvalues as the roots of the characteristic polynomial p(λ) = det(A − λI). The relation Av = λv need only hold for some nonzero eigenvector v, not for every v; and if A − λI were invertible there would be no nonzero solution, so λ could not be an eigenvalue. The last option confuses the eigenvalue (a scalar) with the eigenvector (a nonzero vector).
